questions.question: What is the main purpose of data preprocessing in machine learning?

answers.b: To improve data quality and consistency

explanations.a: Data preprocessing focuses on cleaning and preparing data, not on increasing the number of data samples.
explanations.b: Preprocessing removes noise, handles missing values, and ensures consistency so the data can be effectively used by machine learning models.
explanations.c: Controlling computation speed is not the primary objective of data preprocessing.
explanations.d: Removing all features would eliminate useful information and prevent model training.

questions.question: Which of the following problems is commonly addressed during data preprocessing?

explanations.a: Overfitting is mainly handled during model training and validation, not during data preprocessing.
explanations.b: Model deployment is a post-training activity and not part of data preprocessing.
explanations.c: Handling missing values is a key preprocessing task to ensure data completeness and reliability.
explanations.d: Hyperparameter tuning is performed during model optimization, not during data preprocessing.

questions.question: Handling missing values in a dataset helps to:

explanations.a: Handling missing values reduces noise and improves data quality rather than increasing it.
explanations.b: Properly handling missing values avoids algorithm failures and ensures smooth model training.
explanations.c: The goal is usually to retain data through imputation rather than reducing the dataset size.
explanations.d: Handling missing values does not alter the actual target labels in the dataset.

explanations.b: Target variables are generally not normalized unless required for a specific regression task.
explanations.c: Normalization scales numerical features to a common range, improving model performance.
explanations.d: Class labels represent categories and are not suitable for normalization.

questions.question: Why is normalization important in machine learning?

answers.c: It brings features to a common scale

explanations.a: Converting text into numbers is part of encoding, not normalization.
explanations.b: Removing duplicates is a data cleaning step, not the purpose of normalization.
explanations.c: Normalization ensures all numerical features are on the same scale so no feature dominates the model.
explanations.d: Normalization only rescales existing data and does not increase the number of samples.

questions.question: Encoding is a technique used to:

answers.c: Convert categorical data into numerical form

explanations.a: Dimensionality reduction is achieved using techniques like PCA, not encoding.
explanations.b: Handling missing data is a separate preprocessing step, not the purpose of encoding.
explanations.c: Encoding transforms categorical variables into numerical values that machine learning algorithms can process.
explanations.d: Outlier removal is a data cleaning task and not related to encoding.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a categorical variable?

explanations.a: Age is a numerical variable that represents measurable quantity.
explanations.b: Salary is a numerical variable expressed in continuous values.
explanations.c: Gender represents categories or labels rather than numerical measurements.
explanations.d: Height is a numerical variable measured on a continuous scale.

explanations.b: Feature engineering involves creating new features and transforming existing ones to improve model performance.
explanations.c: Removing entire datasets is not related to feature engineering.
explanations.d: Model deployment is a post-training step and not part of feature engineering.

explanations.a: Model training is carried out using algorithms, not through data visualization.
explanations.b: Encoding is a preprocessing technique and is not performed using visualization.
explanations.c: Data visualization helps in identifying trends, patterns, and relationships within the dataset.
explanations.d: Data visualization does not affect memory usage; it is used for analysis and interpretation.

questions.question: Which step is performed first in a typical machine learning pipeline?

explanations.a: Model evaluation is performed after training to assess model performance.
explanations.b: Model training requires prepared data and therefore cannot be the first step.
explanations.c: Data preprocessing is performed first to clean and prepare data before training the model.
explanations.d: Prediction is done after the model has been trained and evaluated.
